chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wassa, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who testified upon the testimony of another man, so the man came and said, 'I did not appoint him as a witness,' so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony of the more just of the two is valid.'

key_terms.أَعْدَلِهِمَا: the more just of the two

ai.seo_question: How is a witness's testimony validated if the other party claims they were not appointed as a witness?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the jurisprudential mechanism for resolving contradictory testimonies by prioritizing the witness with greater 'adalah' (moral integrity and justice), a core criterion in Shia legal theory. It reflects the practical application of evidentiary standards in early Shia communities, ensuring that judicial decisions rely on the most trustworthy source when direct verification of appointment is disputed. The ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the qualitative assessment of witnesses rather than mere numerical majority.
